content.value_statement: Teams often forget which development skill fits the next step. This skill routes ideas, issues, prototypes, and handoffs into a clear engineering flow.
actual_capabilities: Recommends which Matt Pocock skill to use for idea development, implementation, or maintenance.
Explains when to use interview, prototype, PRD, issue, handoff, and implementation flows.
Shows how to move from a single idea to independent implementation issues.
Guides context-window choices, including when to hand off or compact a session.
Separates incoming issue triage from planned issues that are already agent-ready.
limitations: It does not run the referenced skills for the user.
It only covers the Matt Pocock skill set described in SKILL.md.
It does not inspect a repository or validate issue tracker configuration.
It depends on the user knowing the current work situation clearly.

use_cases.title: Choose the next development step
use_cases.description: A developer can map an idea, bug, or prototype question to the correct workflow skill.

use_cases.title: Plan multi-session implementation work
use_cases.description: A technical lead can decide when to create a PRD, split issues, and start fresh sessions.

use_cases.title: Keep agent work organized
use_cases.description: An AI coding user can preserve context with handoffs and avoid unnecessary triage steps.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a starting skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner user with a broad goal
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a development goal and I am not sure where to start. Use ask-matt to choose the right Matt Pocock skill and explain the next step.

prompt_templates.title: Route an idea to delivery
prompt_templates.scenario: User has an idea that may become implementation work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ask-matt to route this idea through the right flow. Tell me when to interview, prototype, create a PRD, split issues, or implement directly.

prompt_templates.title: Recover from a crowded session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ask-matt to decide whether this session should continue, compact, or move through a handoff. Explain the tradeoff in practical terms.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-session workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user coordinating several agent sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ask-matt to design a multi-session engineering workflow for this project. Include where PRD creation, issue splitting, handoffs, and implementation sessions belong.

output_examples.input: I have a feature idea but many details are unclear.
output_examples.output: Start with the interview flow. Use the documentation-aware path if a codebase exists, then decide whether a prototype is needed before creating a PRD or implementing.

output_examples.input: I already have agent-ready issues from a PRD.
output_examples.output: Skip triage. Start a fresh session for each independent issue and pass the relevant PRD context into the implementation flow.

output_examples.input: This session is near the context limit but the work is not finished.
output_examples.output: Use a handoff when you need a fresh session with preserved context. Use compact only at a clean phase boundary.

best_practices: Describe your current work state before asking for a route.
Keep idea, PRD, and issue creation in one continuous context when possible.
Use a fresh implementation session for each independent issue.
anti_patterns: Do not triage issues that were already created from the PRD flow.
Do not compact in the middle of an active planning phase.
Do not use this router as a substitute for project-specific judgment.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps choose the right Matt Pocock engineering skill or flow for a specific development situation.

faq.question: Does it execute other skills automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends the next skill or flow, but the user still invokes the chosen step.

faq.question: When should I use the PRD path?
faq.answer: Use it when the work is large enough to split into independent implementation issues.

faq.question: When should I use a prototype?
faq.answer: Use a prototype when conversation alone cannot answer a question about state, logic, or visible behavior.

faq.question: How does it handle context limits?
faq.answer: It explains when to keep one session, use a handoff, or compact at a phase boundary.

faq.question: Is this useful outside Matt Pocock skills?
faq.answer: Only indirectly. The guidance is written for the referenced Matt Pocock skill set.
